primitives.name: MCP Server Handshake Verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: The local MCP server builds, starts, handshakes, and dispatches — but it gates every tool behind a freehire token, and no token exists on this VM (creating one is Garrett's act in his own account; none was requested or used).
primitives.assumptions: MCP protocol enforces secure tool access via token-based authorization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon token absence or invalidity during tool invocation.

layer2.mapping: Tool invocation kernel derives from handshake success and token validity, forming GSE's conditional execution logic.
layer2.telemetry: Tool dispatch logs and token validation outcomes.

primitives.name: Fleet Bus Tool Registration
primitives.verbatim_quote: The prepared fleet-bus patch compiles and registers cleanly in a scratch copy of the bus; the live bus was not touched.
primitives.assumptions: Bus registration follows defined schema without modifying live system state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When patch fails compilation or registration schema mismatches.

layer2.mapping: Tool registration mirrors upstream MCP server configuration, enabling GSE to manage tool lifecycles via fleet orchestration.
layer2.telemetry: Patch build artifacts and registration log entries.
